data.why: The app has no file upload; it generates everything from slider parameters via the built-in trained emulator, so no example or synthetic data files are needed.

goals: See how binary eccentricity e_b and mass ratio q_b reshape the morphology of synthetic circumbinary accretion-rate light curves
Draw multiple stochastic realizations at fixed (e_b, q_b) and inspect the mean +/- 1 sigma envelope to gauge aleatoric variability
Toggle epistemic uncertainty on/off to see how much it inflates the predictive spread beyond the aleatoric floor
Convert the emulated accretion rates of M_b, M1 and M2 into LSST AB magnitudes via the alpha-disk blackbody model and check which configurations fall above or below the single-visit detection limit
Scan total mass, binary separation, redshift and Eddington fraction to map which physical regimes would make circumbinary accretion variability observable to LSST
Resample new realizations at the same parameters to distinguish systematic trends from stochastic scatter

review.summary: The tree captures what the calypso demo is for: seeing how e_b and q_b shape the stochastic accretion light curves, checking the aleatoric spread, and judging LSST detectability. Its evidence mostly holds up on the screens. It needs fixes before filing: the setup phase should be removed, the epistemic-uncertainty task and feature misread the code and tested at a grid point where the toggle can't show any effect, and the stated redshift/Eddington-fraction scan is missing.
